questions.prompt: Which part of a yeast cell shows that it is a fungus and not a bacterium?
options: It has a true nucleus
It has a tail for swimming
It has green chlorophyll
It has no cell wall
questions.explanation: Yeast has a true nucleus that holds its DNA, which makes it a fungus. Bacteria have no true nucleus.

questions.prompt: Which substance made by yeast gives tej its alcoholic effect?
options: Lactic acid
Ethanol
Carbon dioxide
Starch
questions.explanation: The wanted product in alcoholic drinks like tej is ethanol, made when yeast ferments sugar without oxygen.

questions.prompt: What does the abbreviation DNA stand for?
options: Double nuclear acid
Digestive nutrient acid
Deoxyribonucleic acid
Dividing natural acid
questions.explanation: DNA stands for deoxyribonucleic acid, the chemical that carries the genetic instructions of living things.

questions.prompt: Which body system uses the brain and nerves to sense and control the body quickly?
options: The excretory system
The skeletal system
The nervous system
The digestive system
questions.explanation: The nervous system, made of the brain and nerves, senses the surroundings and controls the body rapidly.

questions.prompt: Why is a leaf usually broad and flat?
options: To catch as much light as possible
To store large amounts of water
To keep insects away
To pump blood through the plant
questions.explanation: A broad, flat leaf gives a large surface area to absorb the maximum amount of sunlight for photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: Animals such as the Gelada baboon living wild in Ethiopia are an example of which natural resource?
options: Coal
Topsoil
Natural gas
Wildlife
questions.explanation: Wild animals are part of wildlife, a renewable natural resource that must be protected to keep biodiversity.

questions.prompt: In a large factory, yeast is grown in big tanks to ferment sugar into ethanol fuel. Keeping oxygen out of the tank is important because it makes the yeast:
options: Stop reproducing completely
Respire anaerobically and produce ethanol
Turn into bacteria
Release lactic acid instead
questions.explanation: Without oxygen the yeast respires anaerobically (ferments), and this is the reaction that produces the wanted ethanol.

questions.prompt: Before a cell divides, each chromosome is copied so it has two identical halves. What are these two halves called?
options: Genes
Chromatids
Nuclei
Bases
questions.explanation: After copying, each chromosome is made of two identical chromatids, which are later pulled apart during division.

questions.prompt: One strand of DNA has the base order A-C-G-T. What is the matching order of bases on the opposite strand?
options: A-C-G-T
T-G-C-A
G-T-A-C
C-A-T-G
questions.explanation: Using the rules A pairs with T and C pairs with G, the bases A-C-G-T pair with T-G-C-A.

questions.prompt: Of the 23 pairs of chromosomes in a human cell, how many pairs are autosomes (not sex chromosomes)?
options: 23 pairs
22 pairs
1 pair
11 pairs
questions.explanation: Of the 23 pairs, 22 pairs are autosomes and only 1 pair are the sex chromosomes (XX or XY).

questions.prompt: What is the main job of the digestive system?
options: To pump blood to the cells
To break food into small molecules the body can absorb
To remove urine from the blood
To take in oxygen from the air
questions.explanation: The digestive system breaks large food into small soluble molecules, such as glucose, that can be absorbed into the blood.

questions.prompt: Washing hands with soap before eating helps prevent communicable disease mainly because it:
options: Adds vitamins to the food
Makes the body produce insulin
Removes germs from the hands before they reach the mouth
Cools the body down
questions.explanation: Many germs spread from dirty hands to the mouth. Washing with soap removes these germs and stops them being swallowed.

questions.prompt: The small holes (stomata) in a leaf can open and close. This is useful to the plant because it lets the plant:
options: Control gas exchange and water loss
Make chlorophyll faster
Grow new roots overnight
Change carbon dioxide into nitrogen
questions.explanation: Opening and closing the stomata lets the plant take in carbon dioxide while controlling how much water vapour escapes.

questions.prompt: Photosynthesis speeds up as the temperature rises, but only up to a point. Why does it slow down again if it gets too hot?
options: There is suddenly too much light
Very high heat damages the parts of the cell that carry out the reaction
The plant runs out of chromosomes
Carbon dioxide turns into oxygen
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is controlled by delicate proteins (enzymes). Too much heat damages them, so the rate falls instead of rising.

questions.prompt: Why is pollution of a river a serious problem for a community downstream?
options: It makes the water unsafe to drink and harms living things
It adds useful minerals to the drinking water
It increases the number of fish
It turns the water into clean rain
questions.explanation: Polluted water can carry harmful substances and germs, making it unsafe to drink and damaging the plants and animals that live in it.

questions.prompt: A green plant makes glucose during the day. If a leaf cell already has enough glucose for its needs, what does it often do with the extra?
options: Release it as oxygen gas
Turn it into chlorophyll
Store it as starch
Send it back into the air as carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Extra glucose made in photosynthesis is changed into starch for storage, and can be turned back into glucose later when needed.

questions.prompt: Bone is made of many similar cells working together to support the body. At which level of organisation is bone best described?
options: A single cell
A whole organ system
An organ on its own
A tissue
questions.explanation: Bone is a tissue, a group of similar cells working together. Several tissues together (like in a limb) form organs and systems.

questions.prompt: When one cell completes meiosis, how many sex cells are produced?
options: One
Two
Four
Eight
questions.explanation: Meiosis divides twice and produces four sex cells, each with half the chromosome number. Mitosis, in contrast, produces only two cells.

questions.topic: Why injera batter is left to stand
questions.prompt: Teff batter is left for about two days before cooking injera. What happens to the oxygen in the batter during this time?
options: Oxygen is used up, so yeast switches from aerobic to anaerobic respiration
Oxygen is added so the yeast can make ethanol
Oxygen stays the same the whole time
Oxygen turns the batter into lactic acid
questions.explanation: At first the yeast respires aerobically, but as oxygen runs out it switches to anaerobic respiration (fermentation), making the carbon dioxide that raises the batter.

questions.prompt: A sperm with 23 chromosomes joins an egg with 23 chromosomes at fertilisation. How many chromosomes does the new cell (zygote) have?
questions.explanation: The two sex cells each carry 23 chromosomes, so fertilisation joins them to restore the full human number of 46.

questions.prompt: Mendel chose pea plants for his experiments on inheritance. Why were pea plants a good choice?
options: They have no genes to confuse the results
They show clear features such as tall or short and can be bred easily
They grow only in the dark
They reproduce by budding like yeast
questions.explanation: Pea plants have clear, easily seen characteristics (like tall or short) and can be bred in a controlled way, so patterns of inheritance were easy to follow.

questions.prompt: Why is it important that sex cells are made by meiosis, which halves the chromosome number?
options: So each sex cell has double the normal chromosomes
So the sex cells can repair wounds
So the chromosome number stays correct after fertilisation joins two sex cells
So the body grows taller
questions.explanation: If sex cells kept the full number, fertilisation would double it each generation. Halving it in meiosis keeps the species' chromosome number constant.

questions.prompt: After running, a student keeps breathing fast even while standing still. This deep, fast breathing mainly helps the body to:
options: Take in extra oxygen and remove the extra carbon dioxide made by the muscles
Stop the heart from beating
Cool the food in the stomach
Make new red blood cells instantly
questions.explanation: Hard exercise raises respiration in the muscles, so the body breathes faster to supply more oxygen and clear the extra carbon dioxide produced.

questions.prompt: A student breathes out through a straw into clear limewater and it turns cloudy (milky). This shows that breathed-out air contains a lot of:
options: Oxygen
Carbon dioxide
Nitrogen
Water only
questions.explanation: Limewater turns cloudy in the presence of carbon dioxide. Breathed-out air is rich in carbon dioxide because it is a waste product of respiration.

questions.prompt: In a healthy plant, which statement correctly describes the direction substances move in the transport tubes?
options: Xylem carries water upward; phloem can carry food both up and down
Both xylem and phloem carry water downward only
Xylem carries food up; phloem carries water down
Neither tube moves any substance
questions.explanation: Xylem carries water and minerals upward from the roots, while phloem transports dissolved food from the leaves to wherever it is needed, up or down.

questions.topic: Carbon dioxide source for a plant
questions.prompt: When a candle burns inside a sealed jar with a healthy green plant in bright light, the plant can keep making food longer than in an empty jar. The best explanation is that:
options: The burning candle releases carbon dioxide that the plant uses for photosynthesis
The candle gives the plant extra water
The flame replaces the plant's chlorophyll
The candle removes all oxygen the plant needs
questions.explanation: Burning produces carbon dioxide, a raw material for photosynthesis. In the light the plant uses it, so it can keep making food longer.

questions.prompt: Land stripped bare by overgrazing often suffers worse flooding after rain. Why does bare ground increase flooding compared with grassy land?
options: Bare ground turns rain into oxygen
Rain runs off bare ground quickly instead of soaking in
Grass roots block all rainwater
Bare soil absorbs more water than plant-covered soil
questions.explanation: Plant roots and cover help rain soak into the soil. On bare ground the rain runs straight off the surface, so more water rushes away and flooding increases.

questions.prompt: A scientist takes a gene for drought resistance from one plant and inserts it directly into maize cells. How does this differ from selective breeding?
options: It moves a single gene directly, instead of breeding whole organisms over many generations
It uses no genes at all
It is exactly the same as fermentation
It can only be done with animals, never plants
questions.explanation: Genetic engineering moves a chosen gene directly into the organism, giving a fast, precise change, whereas selective breeding crosses whole organisms slowly over generations.

questions.topic: Why white leaf areas make no starch
questions.prompt: In a variegated (green-and-white) leaf tested for starch, only the green parts turn blue-black with iodine. The white parts stay brown because they:
options: Have no chlorophyll, so they cannot photosynthesise
Get no water from the roots
Are too thin to hold iodine
Already contain too much starch
questions.explanation: Only the green parts contain chlorophyll to trap light, so only they photosynthesise and make starch. The white parts make none and stay brown.

questions.prompt: A rural family replaces firewood with a biogas stove fed by animal dung. Besides saving money, why is this also good for conservation?
options: It reduces tree cutting for firewood, helping protect the forest
It uses up the family's drinking water
It releases far more carbon dioxide than burning wood ever could
It removes all bacteria from the soil
questions.explanation: Using biogas means fewer trees are cut for firewood, which helps protect forests and the soil and wildlife that depend on them.

questions.prompt: A father gives one of his two sex chromosomes to each child. Across very many children, roughly what proportion would be expected to be boys?
options: About one quarter
About one half
All of them
None of them
questions.explanation: The father's sperm is equally likely to carry an X (girl) or a Y (boy), so over many children about half are expected to be boys.

questions.prompt: A student tests whether more light increases photosynthesis in a water plant by counting gas bubbles. To make the test fair, the student should change the light but keep:
options: Both the light and the temperature different
Nothing the same
The temperature and the amount of plant the same
A different plant for every light level
questions.explanation: In a fair test only one factor is changed at a time. Here only the light should change, while temperature and the plant are kept the same so they do not affect the result.

questions.prompt: A lizard regrows a lost tail, making many new identical body cells. Which type of cell division builds the new tail, and why?
options: Mitosis, because it makes identical cells for growth and repair
Meiosis, because it halves the chromosome number
Fermentation, because it needs no oxygen
Meiosis, because it makes four different cells
questions.explanation: Repair and growth need new cells identical to the originals, which is done by mitosis. Meiosis is only for making sex cells.

questions.prompt: A patient with severe diarrhoea loses a lot of body water and feels very weak. Giving clean water with salts and sugar helps most because it:
options: Stops the heart from pumping
Replaces lost water and supplies glucose for the cells to use
Removes all bacteria from the gut instantly
Replaces the patient's chromosomes
questions.explanation: Diarrhoea removes water and salts the body needs. A drink of clean water with salts and sugar restores the lost water and gives glucose for the cells to respire.

questions.prompt: A district must decide how to use a hillside that is losing soil. Which plan best protects the soil while still letting farmers grow crops?
options: Plough straight up and down the slope to drain it faster
Remove every plant so crops have no competition
Build terraces and plant trees along the slope, then farm the level steps
Let cattle graze the slope freely all year
questions.explanation: Terracing and trees slow the runoff and hold the soil, so farmers can grow crops on the steps while erosion is reduced. The other options would worsen erosion.

questions.prompt: Both making irgo at home and producing insulin in a factory are biotechnology. What is the key difference between them?
options: Insulin production uses genetic engineering, while making irgo uses natural fermentation by bacteria
Making irgo uses no micro-organisms at all
Insulin production needs sunlight but irgo does not
They both move genes between organisms
questions.explanation: Irgo is traditional biotechnology using natural lactic fermentation by bacteria, while insulin is modern biotechnology relying on genetic engineering to make bacteria produce a human protein.
